hook_text: Every force that can break a structure is something you have done with your own hands this week.
clip_script: There are only four ways to load a bar, and you already know them all. Pull a rope: tension, along the bar, outward. Push a brick: compression, along the bar, inward. Cut paper with scissors: shear, across the bar, opposite ways on each side of the line. Wring a wet cloth: torsion, twisting around the bar. Now find them under a carport. The posts hold the roof up: compression. The diagonal cable stops it racking: tension. The wind shoves the roof sideways and the bolts at the base are sliced: shear. Sheeting fixed on one side lifts in the wind and twists the front beam: torsion. Four members, four forces. On a drawing, straight arrows out, straight arrows in, sideways arrows opposite, curved arrows opposite. Learn the four pictures and you can read any structure on Earth.
visual_style: Four hand actions sketched in quick succession with their arrow symbols; a carport outline appears and each member lights with its arrows.
pacing: Four hand actions in twenty seconds, four carport members in twenty, the four arrow symbols to close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw the arrow symbol for each of the four forces from memory.
